next.reason: The 1985 diagram (§1985:VI.6.16.2) appears to let NEXT SENTENCE be closed by END-IF, but §1985:VI.6.16.3 SR3 forbids it ('If the END-IF phrase is specified, the NEXT SENTENCE phrase must not be specified'), so the 1985 programs are IF with statements and an optional ELSE closed by END-IF, or IF with statements or NEXT SENTENCE and an optional ELSE (statements or NEXT SENTENCE) with no END-IF. §2023:14.9.19.2 states exactly those two shapes, 'Format 1 (delimited)' with END-IF and 'Format 2 (historic)' with NEXT SENTENCE and no END-IF, and the 1985 ellipsis on statement-1 and statement-2 is stated in §2023:14.9.19.3 SR1 ('one or more imperative statements or a conditional statement optionally preceded by one or more imperative statements'). Same programs accepted, same meaning: KEPT (NEXT SENTENCE is archaic in 2023, a standing, not a change). The refusal of NEXT SENTENCE with END-IF stays a compile-time refusal.
